My research sits at the intersection of physical oceanography, data science, and high-performance computing. It is organized around three connected lines: building the data and methods to observe the ocean across scales, using them to understand multiscale physical processes, and tracing how those processes affect ecosystems and human populations.

::: {.research-lines}
[**1 · Data-driven**<br>Fusion, distribution, and interpretation of large ocean datasets](#data){.line-data}

[**2 · Dynamics**<br>Multiscale physical processes in the ocean and atmosphere](#physics){.line-dyn}

[**3 · Impacts**<br>How multiscale physics affects ecosystems and people](#impacts){.line-imp}
:::

## Data fusion, distribution & interpretation {#data}

I develop methods to merge observations from many platforms, distribute them as open, analysis-ready datasets, and interpret them at scale with high-performance and cloud computing.

:::{#list-data}
:::

## Multiscale ocean & atmosphere dynamics {#physics}

I use observations, theory, and numerical simulations to understand physical processes from the mesoscale down to the submesoscale, and their coupling with the atmosphere.

:::{#list-physics}
:::

## Impacts on ecosystems & people {#impacts}

I study how multiscale ocean and atmosphere physics shapes extreme events, marine life, and the communities that depend on them.

:::{#list-impacts}
:::
